item.text:
**Verdict:** mixed, with some real improvement on targeted health, child benefits, education logistics, housing, and water infrastructure, but not a clean case that Putin broadly improved basic welfare in 2023. The strongest counterweight is that food and household affordability worsened under wartime inflation and heavy defense spending.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pro | Expanded free medical care and child/social benefits | Government of the Russian Federation | 9 Jan 2023 | https://government.ru/en/news/47503/ | The government said it added funding for free medical care, expanded primary care and rehabilitation, created special social payments for medical workers, and broadened child-related benefits. This is direct evidence of improved access to health care and social protection. | 6B.2 |
| Pro | Unified child benefit payments on a single day | Social Fund of Russia | 25 Jan 2023 | https://sfr.gov.ru/en/press_center/~2023/01/25/250437 | Child payments were centralized so parents received them on a common delivery date, reducing administrative friction for family support. This supports easier access to social protection. | 6B.2 |
| Pro | Infrastructure budget loans supported housing construction | Government of the Russian Federation | 13 Mar 2023 | https://government.ru/news/47975/ | The government said infrastructure budget credits helped put 5.6 million square meters of housing into service. That is evidence of housing supply support, though it is an input/output claim rather than a direct household-access outcome. | 6B.2 |
| Pro | Clean-water rehabilitation projects | Government of the Russian Federation | 5 Jun 2023 | https://government.ru/en/news/48660/ | The government said water-body rehabilitation projects built or upgraded purification facilities, cut untreated runoff, and improved conditions for millions of residents. This is the best direct evidence found on water and sanitation-related infrastructure. | 6B.2 |
| Pro | 2023 schooling measures: buses, meals, teacher bonuses | Government of the Russian Federation | 2024 retrospective report on 2023 | https://government.ru/en/news/51246/ | The government said nearly 3,000 school buses were delivered in 2023, all primary pupils received free hot meals, and teacher bonuses were expanded. This is strong evidence of better education access and child welfare, though the source is a retrospective government report. | 6B.2 |
| Pro | Poverty fell to 9.3% in 2023 | Reuters | 6 Mar 2024 | https://m.uk.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/poverty-level-in-russia-dropped-to-93-in-2023-says-statistics-service-3368963?ampMode=1 | Rosstat said the poverty rate fell from 9.8% to 9.3% in 2023. That suggests some improvement in material living conditions, though it does not by itself prove better access to specific services. | 6B.2 |
| Con | Families cut back as prices rose | Reuters | 16 Nov 2023 | https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/in-wartime-russia-soaring-prices-bite-as-election-looms-3235923 | Reuters reported that rising prices for baby food, nappies, and other essentials forced families to cut back. This is direct counterevidence on food security and affordability. | 6B.2 |
| Con | Defense spending approached one-third of the budget | Reuters | 5 Oct 2023 | https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/putin-says-russias-economy-can-cope-with-higher-defence-spending-on-war-3191542 | Putin said the economy could absorb much higher defense spending, and Reuters reported defense spending would be close to one-third of the budget. That undercuts a broad welfare-first reading because it implies civilian welfare faced major opportunity costs. | 6B.2 |

**Search gap:** I found strong official evidence on health, education, housing, water, and child benefits, but much of it is government self-report. I did not find robust independent, nationwide outcome data for sanitation quality or nutrition access in 2023, so those subcomponents remain weakly evidenced.
